newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open up $5 to $10 a tonne.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open up $5 to $10 a tonne.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $5 to $10 higher Friday on the heels of a strong performance in London overnight, dealers said.
LIFFE cocoa futures were up sharply early Friday in chart-driven trading. July rose 17 stg by the midday pause to 1,060 stg per tonne, while May stood 16 higher at 1,039 stg.
Speculation that Ivorian shippers were having trouble fulfilling commitments for April and May contracts provided underlying support, London traders said.

Thursday, New York cocoa futures settled broadly higher, but turnover was thin and prices failed to get past key resistance. July futures closed at $1,475 a tonne, up $17 on the day, after sinking to a low of $1,456. Spot May gained $15 to $1,452, while the back months rose $16 to $18.
Technically, filling a chart gap overhead from $1,480 to $1,501 is the next upside objective, traders said.
"We could see a breakout today," said one trader. "Once we get into that gap, we should attract some spec and fund buying."
